name: Manasseh
overview: Manasseh was a male king of Judah and the son of Hezekiah, noted in Scripture for doing evil in the sight of the LORD. His reign is marked by unfaithfulness to God, reflecting a departure from his father's legacy. This profile focuses on his role as a Judahite monarch whose actions had significant spiritual consequences.
namesAndTitles: The name Manasseh means 'one that makes to forget,' highlighting a possible thematic element in his story. Additionally, he held the title 'King of Judah,' which identifies his royal authority and governance over the southern kingdom. Neither name is recorded as given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Manasseh was the son of King Hezekiah and Queen Hephzibah, with Amon identified as his own son. These relationships establish his place within the royal lineage of Judah and link him to both his predecessor and successor on the throne.
scriptureSignificance: Manasseh's reign is significant in the biblical narrative because he continued the royal line of Judah through his father Hezekiah but chose to do evil before the LORD, contrasting with his father's faithfulness. His actions contributed to the spiritual decline of Judah, setting the stage for future judgment. His legacy is intertwined with the history of Judah's kings and their covenantal faithfulness or failure.
